summary: Creates large customizable panel lists whose table, row, column, and cell appearance and interaction are driven by initialization callbacks, event callbacks, and optional drag/drop behavior.

key_params.name: callbacks
key_params.note: Callback DAT that defines list initialize and event behavior

key_params.name: rows
key_params.note: Number of rows in the list

key_params.name: cols
key_params.note: Number of columns in the list

key_params.name: lockfirstrow
key_params.note: Locks the first row while scrolling vertically

key_params.name: lockfirstcol
key_params.note: Locks the first column while scrolling horizontally

key_params.name: offcellcallbacks
key_params.note: Allows callbacks on list areas outside valid cells

key_concepts: List COMP builds large customizable panel lists through initialization and callback functions.
Every table, row, column, and cell is described by callback-assigned attributes.
Rows, columns, locked first row/column, scrollbars, off-cell callbacks, and reset define the list surface and interaction model.
Drag and drop callbacks expose ListCell information with owner, row, and column references.
The Build a List COMP guide is the practical companion for state management, callback ordering, and data-backed list content.
common_gotchas: List COMP content and appearance are not automatic; initialize callbacks must describe cells, rows, columns, and table attributes.
The Build a List COMP article contains the practical callback patterns and should be reviewed for non-trivial lists.
Reset re-runs initialize callbacks, so callback code must be safe to execute repeatedly.
Drag/drop callbacks expose ListCell objects with owner, row, and column; validate indices before using them.
Off Cell Callbacks can generate events with no valid cell under the cursor, so callback code must handle those cases.
Large callback-driven lists can cook heavily if per-cell logic does expensive work.
